h3. Senior Team Lead

The purpose of the Senior Team Lead role is to lead multiple teams of CS People in pursuit of our Customer Support Purpose and role model our expected leadership values and attributes. 


* Demonstrate pursuit of our Customer Support purpose:
** Provide Customer experience feedback to the business so we can improve our products and services.
** Solve Customer issues and make it feel easy so Customers continue to use our products and services.
** Deliver high levels of Stakeholder engagement - giving us the credibility to influence the Customer experience
* Contribute to your Team Lead and Peer success through collaboration, creativity and giving critical constructive feedback.
* Identify problems and opportunities to support our purpose and then initiative, own and contribute to solutions. 
* Ensure your Team Leads and Agents highly engaged 
** Drive clarity of purpose to ensure your people understand their work matters
** Drive a diverse and inclusive environment to ensure all of your people know their opinions matter
** Drive empowerment to ensure all of your people know their decisions matter
** Drive Recognition to ensure all of your people know their contributions matter
** Drive Growth to ensure all of your people know their ambitions matter 
* Lead your Team leads by coaching them to meet their accountabilities
* Role model pursuit of your own accountabilities

h3. ....demonstrate our Leadership values and attributes:

* Drive – our Leaders are hard working, able to tackle large challenges with enthusiasm
* Intelligence – our Leaders are able to learn and solve new problems - they can troubleshoot logically, create scalable and repeatable processes
* Integrity – our Leaders are respectful, ethical and trustworthy
* Empathy - our Leaders can relate to our Customers and their colleagues, they seek to understand different views
* Coach-ability - our Leaders actively seek out, listen to and act on constructive feedback
* Team players - our Leaders collaborate openly and contribute to each others success
* Humility - our leaders don’t need to be the smartest in the room, or be right - they seek out the best decisions and solutions always putting Bolt, and the Team ahead of their own ego
* Growth mindset - our Leaders coach their teams for success, they understand learning from mistakes makes us better Leaders
* Our Leaders build teams with[ |https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LhoLuui9gX8]psychological safety
* Our Leaders create more great Leader

Hey\! Did some background reading, played around with my own app as well, but few things remain unclear.

For starters, my understanding for Work Profile in general is that:

* using Work profile does not require the Passenger account to be added under a B4B Customers Business Account,
* Passenger account (both, Personal and Work profile) however can include a B4B Customers payment method,
* in order to use a Work profile one needs to (a) add an email address where Bolt could send invoices to, and (b) choose a payment method for the trips taken under Work profile,
* currently expense codes nor notes can be added to rides (incl invoices), nor is summary emails supported.

*@mart.parve* please adjust if needed. Also, Work Profile - if used at scale - should be just an interim stop before Customer migrates to Business Portal? To understand the business case. If not, why should a Customer prefer using Work profile over the full functionality of the Business Portal?



Now, to the specifics of the PwC FR case at hand - [@Mariana Figueiredo|mailto:mariana.figueiredo@bolt.eu] and/or @mart.parve please confirm:


* PwC shall not sign up for access to the Business Portal, incl shall not enter the B4B Agreement under the T&C.
* PwC shall:
** provide a list of emails of employees who shall sign up for a regular Bolt Passenger account and create themselves a Work profile. _What if the Passenger already has a Bolt Passenger account connected to his/her phone No, or s/he wants to have a Passenger account for private purposes? Does this employee need to have more than one phone No? Why don't we agree instead that PwC shall just provide a list of emails which their employees add to their Work profile for sending the invoices to, and we'll use this as basis for any further invoicing, cashbacks etc?_
** pay for the rides done using the email address named above by using the postpayment payment method as described in clause 4.17 etc in the B4B T&C. _Or is there a reason why we do not want or need to agree on the exact payment method up front?_
* Bolt shall:
** provide PwC a summarizing report (incl data on total No of trips and total amount of Fare) for all the Work profile rides done under respective Passenger accounts. 
** provide a 3% cashback for a full calendar year of cooperation _(i.e no cashback if Agreement has lasted less than one full calendar year in any way? So PwC gets cashback if the agreement is valid from Jan 1st 2021 to Dec 31st 2021, but not if from Jan 2nd 2021 to Dec 30th 2022?_) by 31st of January of n+1
** provide -30% of discount for all PWC employees on their non Work profile rides for the first 5 trips taken (available for the 1st 3 months since respective comms - i.e _push notification? I trust we have log to prove the time of such push?_). _Is it at all doable if the Passengers are required to sign up for a separate Passenger account?_

And as heads up, the above necessarily doesn't cover all the details yet. Legal has not facilitated Work profile in such manner before, but I expect we're able to reuse B4B T&C in many aspects though, foremost clause 4 (Payments), but also for personal liability, term and termination, final provisions, data processing, confidentiality. 

Yet all in all requires drafting a contract from scratch.

Before the above is cleared it's impossible to provide any ETA's, but I understand the aim is to get this up and running very latest by January 1st? [~accountid:5f646960f4571b006a821de7] 


In terms of language let's keep to EN for now. In the end we can of course translate the legal documentation to FR as well if business requires.

[~accountid:5fa118a781b2880078eb0e6f] for background - the rules around direct marketing come from e-privacy directive which is transferred to local laws, not gdpr. it mainly foresees that consent should be used for direct marketing but there is an exception that we use. if we get user’s contact detail on providing our service, then we can send them marketing messages without consent but only messages that relate to our own same or similar products (the so called soft opt-in). but of course, the user has to have the possibility to unsubscribe at any time.

So the direct marketing is done correctly via soft opt-in but there was just a mistake with unsubscribing.

Armin, your product assumptions are correct.

As for “why this solution”, then we don’t support the “individual credit cards for employees of one Business customer” case. This is planned for 2021 but it’s a tricky project and thus impossible before EOQ1, and probably more like Q2-Q4.

Currently, the scenarios contemplated by Ops are explicitly *not supported* by Product:

* Business Portal with individual credit cards: Not working at all
* Many Business Portal accounts for one Company (one for each employee): Will break reporting in some places; suspect to fraud check false positives; no central rides reporting; not possible to identify which invoice documents belong to which user and on our end which company belongs to which employee (unless user name or code added to the legal Company Name); possibly other drawbacks and risks. With Business Portal, we have at least email validation, thus we have control over who is enrolling in the scheme.
* “Affiliated” Work Profiles (Customer supplying a list of enrolled email addresses, us filtering the rides for these accounts and calculating kickbacks): We have no way to control who is enrolling in the scheme; it’s very easy to mistakenly select a personal payment method for Work Profile rides, and we have no way of making it right retroactively.

While it is conceivable to go for an “ops hack” here with either of the last 2 options, it’s risky one way or another. *Thus, legally the service should be “as is”, and commercially, there’s a risk of customer dissatisfaction.*

Also, with the work profile hack, we have no watertight method of controlling who is enrolling in the scheme. I can’t see any incentive to misrepresent oneself in the portal as a PWC France, but just that there is no technical control over that.

Thanks for clarifying Samuel\!

We have actually dealt with a similar incident before and given advice on this (I believe it was in EE). I will repeat the general principle here, but it would be useful if this could be amended into CS/ops processes to avoid confusion moving forward. 👍 

While the physical scooter when not active is our responsibility, anyone seeking to claim damage would have to *prove* this damage was caused by the scooter. This photo alone does not prove the scooter caused this damage. In such cases where there is no clear evidence to support the claim (ie: video showing rider on the trip actually doing this) then it is certainly risky for us to assume and draw any conclusions. 

Otherwise, as you can imagine, everyone with little bumps in their car would be framing scooter accidents to make insurance claims for free repair 🙂 

Presuming your investigation does not turn up any clear evidence showing how the incident happened, your response to the car owner will need to be one explaining our free-floating parking model and asking them to please let us know if they have further evidence to provide. We cannot make any conclusions here. We should avoid any elective compensation in such cases as well as it would only service to create a standard that we do so and could show us accepting ‘liability’ where we do not wish to.

Since these kinds of claims can be risky if escalated from a PR perspective, I would advise that you run the response past the PR team for due diligence. If the driver chooses to come back and escalate the issue then we will consider and respond accordingly. 

Hope this helps\!

A lot of drivers in our fleet have arrangements with fleet partners for their vehicles. We’ve devised a solution to directly work with fleet companies and allow them to provide us documentation directly. We will be giving fleet companies access to a fleet partner portal for uploading documents. Drivers are only unblocked once their new vehicle and documents are approved. 
Given that these systems are not in place in the partner portal, the alternate measure is to ensure fleet companies provide new vehicle documentation before the driver is given the vehicle (at least 24 hours in advance) so that we may review and approve the documents ahead of time.

I would like to demonstrate something and get feedback. 

On report scooter page, we have image upload for desktop, “open camera” and “choose from gallery” for mobile devices. And “open camera“ is for only Android users. Iphone users will see only one button “Upload Photo“ and when it is clicked it shows 3 options: {{Photo Library, Take Photo, Browse}}. It is OS specific thing. 

!photo5940292065516696617.jpg|width=750,height=1231!

So my concern is about Android devices case and open camera. On [godparkering.no|http://godparkering.no] page when open camera is clicked it embeds a video inside the container and captures a photo with it. 



!t_video5364056356158441758.mp4|width=1080,height=1920!


We had the same approach. But it takes some time to have a similar feature as quite many things should be implemented such as a new view, capturing a photo which is base64, and converting it to File object in order to use the same way as image upload works.  As time is the essence for the report scooter page I would prefer not to implement the same thing but take a different approach. So when “Open Camera” is clicked Android native camera opens, the user takes a photo and uses it. So it automatically is appended to the file list. 



!t_video5364056356158441756.mp4|width=1080,height=1920!

So in this way we don’t think about any other corner cases. As this opening camera is for only Android devices (Iphone has own way), it would be better to use opening Android native camera and not implement another view for it. So that we would deliver it on time.

+I Re MSA+, Transcom has not only limited the liability for confidential obligation violation, but *Transcom’s has limited its liability in full* *for all violations and this is unacceptable*.  Please see clauses 6.5 and 8.6 of the MSA.

Clause 6.5: Re the contractual penalty for confidentiality obligation breach. The new wording proposed by Transcom states that *full liability* for the breach is limited to 100% annual value. This is not the purpose of contractual penalty concept. Contractual penalty should work as follows: If Transcom violates the confidentiality obligation, then we can claim the contractual penalty in the amount of 100% of the annual contract value. In case the breach has caused Bolt damages higher than the amount of contractual penalty, then Bolt has the right to claim compensation in addition to the contractual penalty *to the extent not covered by the contractual penalty.* Therefore, the current wording is not suitable and initial wording should remain, but we can agree with the amount of contractual penalty to be 100% of the annual contract value.

Clause 8.6 – Transcom’s *full liability* is limited to 100% fees paid. This is not acceptable, because damages Transcom could cause Bolt can be lot higher.

_In case of doubt whether any information made available to the Employee constitutes the Employer’s business secret, the Employee must treat it as the Employer’s business secret and is required to ask Employer’s opinion at least in the reproducible form about its confidentiality before using such information._

[~accountid:557058:248ddbe5-09e7-4270-91a4-c46e757ead14], a few points to discuss:

# Default etcd quota (max db size) is 2G.  Do you think we need larger? https://etcd.io/docs/v3.2.17/dev-guide/limit/

A: No, 2G should be plenty, Vitess has very low traffic and other etcd clusters in production with much higher workload are running fine with such size.

# Etcd needs regular compaction to free up old versions of KVs (https://etcd.io/docs/v3.2.17/op-guide/maintenance/#history-compaction). This can be manually done or automatically scheduled by etcd if enabled with: https://etcd.io/docs/v3.2.17/op-guide/configuration/#--auto-compaction-retention
I think we should enable this so we don't have to manually compact. Do you agree? How often do you think? Thoughts welcomed. 

A: Since we don't expect to use a lot of disk space, compaction should not be a frequent operation. Maybe once or twice a year if even that. 

# Due to period compacting, etcd DB also needs occasional defrag, which is blocking. The frequency of defrag will be less than compact, but I expect it will still need to be done once in a while. For now, I suggest we do it manually, in rotating fashion (followers then leaders) until there is enough experience/sensibility to look into automating, eg: https://www.compose.com/articles/how-to-keep-your-etcd-lean-and-mean/
https://etcd.io/docs/v3.2.17/op-guide/maintenance/#defragmentation

A: Defrag should be even less needed due to same reason as compaction.

This is high risk health data and, ideally, we don’t want to be routinely touching it. There is a host of enhanced legal safeguards required and, speaking frankly, we’re not equipped to process this data - it constitutes ‘special category’ under the GDPR. 

Instead, customers should be relying on local track and trace systems/the Covid Exposure App established by their government/local health authorities. 

I advise CS  write up a standard response. Something like:

Thank you for contacting Bolt and making this voluntary disclosure to us.  We will now take any necessary actions to help protect the health interests of others. We encourage you, if you haven’t done so already, to download your local Covid Exposure App which is usually made available by your country’s health authority. \[END]

I advise against blocking users who confirm they are positive. And we shouldn’t ask for test results. The guidance on whether or not to use a Bolt service is in wider public health announcements and safety/behavioural flags we also share in-App. The action instead, I advise, is one of being a good corporate citizen: notify the driver(s) - without sharing any personal data of the passenger - that they may have been in proximity with a passenger who has since tested positive for Covid.

* Sample backup script for ideas. This is from non vitess etcd servers at Bolt.

{code:bash}
/etc/cron.scripts/backup-etcd-datadir.sh

#!/bin/sh

hostname=$(hostname)

working_dir=/var/lib/etcd
backup_data_dir=$working_dir/backup
prev_bak=$working_dir/previous

etcd_home=/dev/shm/etcd
data_dir=$etcd_home/$hostname

if [ ! -d $data_dir/member ]; then
        exit
fi

if [ -d $backup_data_dir ]; then
        rm -rf $prev_bak
        mkdir $prev_bak
        mv $backup_data_dir $prev_bak
        mkdir $backup_data_dir
fi

etcdctl backup \
 --data-dir $data_dir \
 --backup-dir $backup_data_dir

cp -p $data_dir/member/snap/db $backup_data_dir/member/snap

Maintenance task
1. Creating DB objects
  - Creating schema
  - Creating service users
  - Creating tables

* Key points
You have a certain rules for creating schema and service users and tables.
Some of rules are just naming rules but some rules are directly impacting performance and maintenance.
For example,
we are not allowed to create foreign keys, triggers for use of gh-ost.
We are not allowed to create procedures for performance and monitoring.
We check index very carefully.
We check the requested PK type. 1. Only integer type 2. Only unsigned.
We check unique key type. 1. Is unique key column nullable or not 2. If it is nullable, check the reason.
We check index efficiency by checking SELECT queries as well.
If there are any limiting facts for vitess specific, then it will be very good to know.

2. Altering tables
  - Add column
  - Drop column
  - ADD index
  - Drop index
  - Rename table
  - Rename column ( It is very rare but still developers make requests )
  - Change column types ( Usually adding additional enum value, change from small type to bigger one like int to bigint, varchar to text so on )
  - Setup new AUTO_INCREMENT value ( It is also rare but we have done it few times )

3. Dropping big tables
  - It is not a frequent operation but usually, we consider a dangerous operation because it locks MySQL process while it performs.
    I understand Tarmo mention about garbage collection feature in vitess so I am counting on it.

4. Dropping schema
  - Very rare but we get this time to time

5. Query tuning and indexing
  - Sometimes developers ask about query tuning and indexing, usually, this is Andre's field but I also do this from time to time.
    Are there any vitess specific feathers we should know about? For example, running explain, profile

6. MySQL version up & building a new version images
  - This is another rare operation but when you confirm a bug in the current version, we perform the operation.


Troubleshooting task

1. Fix broken replication
  - Data inconsistency cases like duplicate key, Data missing for update / delete, user missing cases
  - Errant GTID case
  - Changing replication topology when the intermediate master fails ( Usually, simple we changing the topology by Orchestrator, not a big deal but the operation is quite frequent )

2. Master fail case

3. Slave / sandbox re-creation
  - This is quite a frequent operation where there is disk or file system failure. I remember from the first hands-on, it is even easy for vitess to create a slave. I am counting on it.

4. Deadlock and finding and killing long-run query 
  - Are there any specific vitess feature we should know about?

5. Backup & Restore strategy.
  - I remember from the first hand-on session but it will be very nice we could use written documentation

What I means is that legally some portions of the goods / services that eater acquires on a platform are indeed exposed to a 30-day complain period (mandated by law). Hence the sec. 5.1 repeating what some consumer laws say. However, you are also right that 30 days is too long of a term to solve effectively majority of food related issue and thus we aim users to report things swiftly and guide towards this in our FAQ entry. Also not all the portions of service pack are required to bear a 30-day complaint period, although at the moment our T&Cs do not make it clear.

My proposal:

* how to view in general: 30 day period is a legal backstop. We are obliged to take user complaints that come within 30 day period from the order moment. At least until we update our T&Cs and make it more specific in which cases we take within 30 days and in which cases within some shorter term;
* FAQ: it is ok to have FAQ gently pushing eaters to react swiftly while case is still “hot” 🙂 This is in the interest of all -  Bolt, Restaurant and Eater. However, I would change tone of the FAQ entry slightly to lessen the impression that complaints coming after 12 hr mark will be ignored. And indeed I would propose to have this update across all BF market entries.

Let me know if this is helpful. And will add this point to a list of more “urgent” updates to our BF T&Cs.

Julius

Hi Armand,

In general I suggest to approach and discuss this with Commerce team if they have such an option to refund directly to the mean of payment OR as a bank transfer.

From legal side (speaking here with no facts of the case in general sense): if she paid for something she did not receive or had a claim against bad / failed service that we acknowledged as such and thus a case for refund arose → she is right, funds should come back to her in same form she paid. The tricky part is that strictly legally Restaurant - not Bolt has to do that. But that is extremely poor UX sending to deal with rest directly outside Bolt.

So we try to find mid-ground:

* if possible to make refund as requested → should make it.
* if not ->we can apologies, can point to is our T&C sec. 5.2 (it says that refund may be made or Bolt Balance issued) and give a Bolt balance explaining that Bolt cannot do anything else but issue a balance,  as no functionality is here and that of course she has a claim towards restaurant directly if she chooses. Also may consider larger BB than the refund amount.

The bottom line here is that if the order is fulfilled partially while the full amount is paid - eater absolutely has a right to get back the difference. Although Restaurant is ultimately responsible for this - we do not want to keep users out in a dark and have to step in. The only defendable refund mechanic is giving back money and the fact that we cannot technically do this (if that is the case) is on us. And our offer to give BB instead although mentioned in the T&Cs - is not defendable and is more at a mercy of user than our legal right.

Furthermore, resale of B4B is regulated in 4.6 of [global T&C of B4B|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/terms-for-business/] as follows:

"*4.6.*  .... In countries determined by Bolt, the Customer may select a resale invoicing model, whereby the issuer of invoices and recipient of the payments, including additional fees charged in connection with the model, is a company that acts as a reseller (Reseller) of rides taken by Users under Business Account. *Bolt Operations OÜ*, *another affiliate of Bolt*, or *third party appointed by Bolt* may act as the Reseller. Section 5 and all other limitations of liability of Bolt provided in these Terms and Conditions shall apply respectively (mutatis mutandis) to the Reseller, unless specifically stipulated otherwise."

{color:#ff5630}*REVISED PROPOSED RESPONSE*{color}

Dear \[INSERT NAME],

Thank you for contacting Bolt again on \[INSERT DATE].

My name is Calum Liddle, and I have recently joined Bolt as the Data Protection Officer. You're likley aware that the DPO is mandated to provide advice to, on my part, Bolt, on its data protection obligations, including those under the General Data Protection Regulation. The DPO may also be contacted by data subjects, such as yourself, with regards to exercising rights, including the right of subject access.

To that extent I have reviewed the correspondence to date between yourself and Bolt with regards to your enquiries around processing activities and your request for subject access. I also consulted relevant staff in the business. My response now follows.

You asked for Bolt to provide: 

\[1] An alternative disclosure format other than a ".json" file.

I looked into providing an alternative format bearing in mind the perceived limitations you mentioned of a disclosure in the ".json" format.

To make a conversation to PDF ensures that the disclosure is illegible in any event, and over 700 pages long. It would fail to satisfy the requirements to provide you with a disclosure of that which constitutes "personal data" for the purposes of the GDPR. I would stress that Bolt is only obligated to disclose that which is defined as personal data held. The GDPR requires that information be provided to you in a concise, transparent, intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language. There is, however, no obligation to make illegible records legible, nor to translate information.

Bolt has previously said that, in any event, the "json" file is a common format which can be used by laypersons. I have undertaken a cursory search on the internet and I'm satisfied that this is indeed the case. It is widely described online as a "very common data format" and is freely accessible. Furthermore, staff here have tested this themselves and shown that a file in this format can be downloaded quite easily by those with non-technical/non-computing backgrounds, and opened.


You also asked for Bolt to provide:


\[2] A disclosure of the "reasons for account blocking". You said it was "also essentially to receive information about logic used by your automated tools when the decision to block was made."

Bolt has already confirmed the account was suspended on suspicion of fraudulent activity. The account remains suspended on a separate issue related to identity verification, a requirement under data protection law itself to ensure appropriate technical safeguards are maintained (although this is a separate issue I will not address in this response).

The account, as stated, was not blocked in perpetuity. We have human review systems in place which are alerted to accounts at risk, or suspended due to suspected breaches of terms, conditions or policies, and for legal and regulatory purposes also, including fraudulent activity. This is a procedure Bolt follows in order to uphold organisational and technical safeguards required, no less, under the GDPR.

The "reason for account blocking", as you put it, has therefore been disclosed to you. It follows this part of your request has been fulfilled here.

Turning to the request for logic, Bolt refuses to disclose the logic used in suspending or blocking accounts more generally. It is well known that technology companies, including Bolt, and those that process financial data, for example, use rules and logic to help determine whether a user's account is at such risk, or in breach of policy, that which might warrant suspension in order to protect the integrity and safety of the user and/or others.

Processing activities are already made transparent by way of the user facing Privacy Policies made readily available. Bolt also publishes behavioural expectations of drivers and riders in terms and conditions. And there are a series of self-help articles available also. These can be inspected by anyone online.

Disclosure of the logic would reveal information concerning Bolt's safety, welfare and fraud prevention mechanisms - and, crucially, their thresholds. It could lead to individuals so inclined to calculate the effectiveness of those mechanisms. Releasing logic, even partially in response to individual data subject requests, is a risk: For example, disclosure may allow a person to infer Bolt suspension thresholds, and provides a key to bad actors who may be inclined to 'game the system' or, in other words, endeavour to gain immunity from their efforts to break the law, defraud or breach terms, etc. Bolt's attempts to protect accounts, users and its wider business activities would be prejudiced.

On weighting of the rights and freedoms of others, including the increased risk to other users and their safety, account integrity, and Bolt's own commercial interests in protecting its enterprise, the company moves to refuse a disclosure concerning logic.

I trust this explanation, while disappointing to you, is at least helpful in providing the reassurance sought around Bolt's processing activities.This is Bolt's final response on the matter.

Lastly, you mentioned your intention to approach the Latvian DPA. Our lead supervisory authority is the Estonian Data Protection Inspectorate. You have the right to approach the Estonian Data Protection Inspectorate in order to appeal this decision at: [https://www.aki.ee/et|https://www.aki.ee/et]


Best wishes,



Calum Liddle

Erki,

 

According to the Clause 5, Article 1 of the Law on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorism and Proliferation Financing (AML Law), UBO definition is following:

_beneficial owner - a natural person who is the owner of the customer - legal person - or who controls the customer, or on whose behalf, for whose benefit or in whose interests business relationship is being established or an individual transaction is being executed, and it is at least:_

_a) regarding legal persons - a natural person who owns, in the form of direct or indirect shareholding, more than 25 per cent of the capital shares or voting stock of the legal person or who directly or indirectly controls it;_

_b) regarding legal arrangements - a natural person who owns or in whose interests a legal arrangement has been established or operates, or who directly or indirectly exercises control over it, including who is the settlor, the trustee or the protector (manager) of such legal arrangement._

 

In addition, according to the AML Law, legal entities should provide following information on their UBO: given name, surname, personal identity number (if any) and the date, month, and year of birth, number of the personal identification document and date of issue thereof, country and body issuing the document, nationality, country of residence, as well as the manner of exercising control over the legal person or foreign subject, including by indicating the given name, surname, personal identity number (if the person has no personal identity number - date, month, year of birth) of a shareholder (stockholder), member or owner through which the control is exercised, but, if it is a legal person - the firm name, registration number, and registered address, as well as the documentary justification of the control exercised.

 

Please let us know if you have any update of information about UBO which we should provide to the SRS.

4 - Deploy etcd backup script

root@etcd-2:~# mkdir /etc/cron.scripts

# backup script for etcd global cluster (vitess)
# /etc/cron.scripts/backup-etcd.sh
#!/bin/sh

hostname=$(hostname)
working_dir=/var/lib/etcd
backup_data_dir=$working_dir/backup
prev_bak=$working_dir/previous

etcd_home=/var/lib/etcd
data_dir=$etcd_home/default

s3_bucket=bolt-vt-backups
s3_path=live-ib/etcd-global

# if etcd data is not present, abort backup
if [ ! -d $data_dir/member ]; then
        exit
fi

# keep one and only one copy of previous backup
if [ -d $backup_data_dir ]; then
        rm -rf $prev_bak
        mkdir $prev_bak
        mv $backup_data_dir $prev_bak
        mkdir $backup_data_dir
fi

# backup etcd (this copies both v2 and v3 data)
etcdctl backup \
 --data-dir $data_dir \
 --backup-dir $backup_data_dir

# also needs this file otherwise restore will fail
cp -p $data_dir/member/snap/db $backup_data_dir/member/snap

# Compress, etcd data has high compression ration
backup_tarfile=etcd-global-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M).tar.gz
/bin/tar cfvz $etcd_home/$backup_tarfile $backup_data_dir

# Upload to S3 - directory name is date+hour+minute
aws s3 cp $etcd_home/$backup_tarfile s3://$s3_bucket/$s3_path/

# Remove tarball after upload to s3
if [ -f $etcd_home/$backup_tarfile ]; then
        rm $etcd_home/$backup_tarfile
fi
{noformat}

* Paying the amount agreed to be owed;

Hi Robinson.

discussed with legal team the DashBoard cam project and potential data privacy-scope and implications.

The short high-level message is that for Bolt collecting raw video-data from street level is potentially associated with high privacy-risk ask we may end up holding and processing highly sensitive personal data (god know what dash-cams will capture). 

This means that we may need to go through a process that is called Data Protection Impact Assessment to document this properly. This is a GDPR process that we cannot avoid even if data is collected outside EU as once data hits our servers in EU - GDPR standards apply. Such thing is very time-consuming and complex and may take around 2 month. Most taxing part is that it has to be done before Bolt collect data.

BUT - this is super high level framework without having checked the details - > most importantly set-up of our arrangements with third parties that we will collab with. To be more specific:

* are they deploying dashboard cams and collecting video imagery directly from them?
* what kind of personal data processing safe-guards they have in place: auto blur of faces, etc.
* what would our arrangement look like with them (we assume that if these entities have done this before they prob have standards and processes in place that we can rely on).

So all in all it is best we start talking with the partners, understand what could be the arrangement/framework; analyze any safeguards and once have this - will make a call if we need Data Protection Impact Assessment at all. And if yes - what is the most effective way to do this (in-house or outsource to highly experienced external advisor).

Also once the proposed set-up with the partners is clearer (in particular who owns and deploys dashboard cams - us or them) we can determine if we need local advise in each city about any licenses or so to be collecting data (it is more clear for us in EU so Vilnius, Riga, Paris - and less so in Ryiad and Jhnbrg).

I propose let’s set a call for us to discuss this portion and plan next steps.

*Problem 1*:

explore: *clevertap_control_group_users* [https://taxify.eu.looker.com/projects/marketing/files/clevertap.model.lkml|https://taxify.eu.looker.com/projects/marketing/files/clevertap.model.lkml]

has join with both *company_order* and *rental_order (aka rental.order_order).* Also it has join with *currency_exchange_rates* via *company_order* and *currency_exchange_rates_rental* (aka *currency_exchange_rates*).

When I add *sum_of_price_eur* metric from *rental_order* Looker throws an error: _Non-Unique value/primary key (or sql_distinct_key), value overflow or collision when computing sum_

Reason for error: several one-to-many connections in one explore. 

*Solution and problem 2*:

How to fight it: [https://help.looker.com/hc/en-us/articles/360037732513-Error-Non-Unique-value-primary-key-or-sql-distinct-key-value-overflow-or-collision-when-computing-sum|https://help.looker.com/hc/en-us/articles/360037732513-Error-Non-Unique-value-primary-key-or-sql-distinct-key-value-overflow-or-collision-when-computing-sum] (last paragraph ‘What If None of the Listed Causes Apply, but the Error Still Occurs?’)

After I create a combined PK, error dissapeared, but new problem appeared: muplitplication of data. Say, one user with *sum_of_price* 5 eur had *sum_of_price_eur* 500 eur, if he had ride-hailing rides in 100 different days.

This is because *sum_of_price_eur* metric in rental.order_order uses *currency_exchange_rates* table, which is already joined to *clevertap_control_group_users* explore (via *company_order*). That means that when I select *sum_of_price_eur* from *rental.order_order,* Looker silently joins *company_order* as well and multiplicates data.

*Solution 2*:

Created *sum_of_price_eur_lifecycle* metric in rental.order_order and explicitly made it use *currency_exchange_rental* view, joined to *clevertap_control_group_users.*

Deleted metric *sum_of_price_eur_lifecycle* from all rental explores so that absence of join with *currency_exchange_rental* in rental model does not lead to data integrity issues. Done it using fields notation:

fields: \[ALL_FIELDS*,
-order_order.sum_of_price_eur_lifecycle]

Hi guys

This is a good example of an agreement which we do not want to sign (includes high number of clauses that we want to change or add) and why we need to push the landlords to use our template. My comments are following:

*Location of premises*: not clear for me, if we rent the entire building or only part of the building, as there is nothing in the agreement clarifying it. If we rent only part of the building, the contract must provide us with a size of the premises and include an annex describing the location of the premises.

*Permitted use*: I did not find a clause saying for what purposes we can use the premises. Shall be added and described clearly.

*Parking slots*: it does not come out from the agreement that we are also entitled to use parking slots, where is the location of the parking slots and what is the rent for using these. Shall be added.

*List of accessory expenses*: the agreement does not include an exhaustive list of the additional services that we are obliged to pay for (i.e. there is an open list), and therefore, the accessory expenses cannot be predicted. The agreement says that we pay 350 EUR in advance each month, but it does not mean that our obligations are limited with that cost, as the agreement says explicitly that we pay also for local taxes, repairing building, etc. We should pay only for services that can be measured (electricity, water, heating) and rest of the cost should be included in the rent. This should be said out in the agreement explicitly. The landlord knows his property and can adjust the rent, if there are some ongoing expenses, that he wants us to incur. In sense of amending the agreement it means that chapter 3 should in large extent be deleted and replaced with wording available in our template.

*Term of the agreement*: should be 1 year or 2 years with a right to terminate the lease agreement as of 12 months have passed with an advance notice of 1-2 months. Automatic renewal should be excluded, as in practice we do not remember that we can exclude it under certain terms.

*Subleasing*: chapter 11 should be amended in a way that the landlord acknowledges that we use subcontractor to maintain and deploy the scooters and when the premises are used by such subcontractor, it is not deemed as sublease in sense of this agreement. Alternative is that we do not have to ask their consent for subleasing the premises.

*Deposit*: chapter 8 should state clearly latest when the deposit is returned to us (max 1 month after the end of the lease agreement).

*Landlords right to pledge our assets located in the premises*: chapter 9 should say the opposite it is saying at the moment, i.e. the landlord should waive its right to have a pledge on our property (scooters), otherwise they there is a chance that they can block our operations at one point. This is must be amendment.

*Winter maintenance*: according to chapter 14 it is our obligation, but it should be landlord obligation, as in practice we do not want to be responsible for common areas. (parking slots are part of the lease object and not part of common areas).

*State of the premises when handing premises over to us*: Chapter 1 subclause 3 says that we have used the same premises previously, which is wrong and should be deleted.

*Electricity*: the agreement should clearly state what electricity power is granted to us by the landlord and that any obstacle regarding using electricity is equated as an obstacle regarding using premises.

*Access to premise by landlord*: should be allowed only in case the landlord informs us 72 hours in advance or there is emergency which requires accessing.

*Confidentiality*: the agreement should include confidentiality clause (every info/data received during performing obligations under the agreement is confidential).

Pleas also note that he landlord’s liability is limited with intention and gross negligence, which is almost impossible to prove.

As the agreement requires many principal changes, please consider asking the landlord to use our template.

Best regards,
Kaija

Hi all,

*In general it's a rather classical health insurance, i.e insurance to cover regular medical expenses. The contract drafting as such is also ok.*

I trust @uche has already approved this, but if not yet then @uche you'll have the chance to confirm the latest at the time you'd be signing this as the director of Bolt NIG. Once the below is cleared and no further issues raised from either of the parties I'd send you the final doc via Hellosign for e-signature as according to the agreement it can be signed not only electronically, but also in counterparts, i.e the process is made very convenient.

However, *before moving to any signatures we need to clear the following:*

* As I understand the yearly premium to be paid shall be ca EUR 28k. Such agreement *needs also prior approval from* *@karin.palmquist* *as CFO's rep, unless it's already budgeted/ approved*. [~accountid:5fc5f6effacfd600762bcb29] please confirm.
* Even though the commercial owner can be considered to be @uche I trust he would not be the *daily contact* in terms of administrating this contract. Either would be @Femi I suppose? That leaves you [~accountid:5fc5f6effacfd600762bcb29] *? Please confirm. The following is foremost for you.*
* The *precise benefits included* - that detail is for you [~accountid:5fc5f6effacfd600762bcb29] to confirm whether what is proposed by Axa matches our needs.
* Same goes i*n general for making sure that we fully benefit from the insurance cover*, i.e all the formalities for enrolling the employees are met (see e.g clause No 6), making sure we do not miss the renewal deadline etc. [~accountid:5fc5f6effacfd600762bcb29] 
* Please also *check with the Accounting team* that Axa would get our *correct invoicing address* [~accountid:5fc5f6effacfd600762bcb29] 
* as a rather specific item in clause 9 there is a reference to *liability insurance taken up by Axa* _against any liability for damage or death or personal injury arising from the provision of the services to any beneficiary arising under the medical scheme_.  [~accountid:5fc5f6effacfd600762bcb29] please ask Axa to elaborate *what this is about* exactly (as Axa itself does not provide any medical service as such) and *how Bolt or any beneficiary would benefit from this* should any relevant event occur.
* Last but not least I'm *including our privacy counsel* [~accountid:5ecceffac761b10c33d5ba08] to this ticket. For background, we do already have health insurance in place in several countries around the world (largely historic pieces), but this is the first which has come in for a proper legal review, and as it is a rather big (and non EU) piece capturing all NIG staff then I trust it's an appropriate point to think the privacy aspects through in detail. [~accountid:5ecceffac761b10c33d5ba08] *please guide should you need any additional information from* [~accountid:5fc5f6effacfd600762bcb29]*, me or anyone else.* Below are my first thoughts.

The way I understand it in EU such health insurance is a rather straightforward matter in terms of personal (sensitive) data processing. Insurers are deemed as data controllers and have the relevant GDPR compliant legal basis and processes to process the health data. [~accountid:5ecceffac761b10c33d5ba08] see Estonia's Insurance Activities Act § 217 and beyond as a rather thorough example of this (especially § 218  [https://www.riigiteataja.ee/en/eli/511122019006/consolide|https://www.riigiteataja.ee/en/eli/511122019006/consolide]). However, likely we won't find similar legal wording in NIG law. Even though the approach should remain the same. [~accountid:5ecceffac761b10c33d5ba08] *would already that aspect trigger the need for a controller-controller data processing agreement from our side, or similar?* There is just section 14 in the agreement, but it's rather narrow.

Secondly, by default the policyholder (Bolt) should not be managing any or at least not systematically employee's health data during the administration of this insurance arrangement, hence whatever personal data processing what needs to be done from our side, e.g in relation to enrollment of employees would be done on the regular employer-employee legal basis. [~accountid:5ecceffac761b10c33d5ba08] I *hope you can elaborate on how we’re approaching similar issues in general today, and whether it is sufficient to facilitate such health insurance related processing as well.* 
[~accountid:5fc5f6effacfd600762bcb29] from your side *please confirm that Bolt would not be systematically processing any personalized employee health data as such.* The contract draft in general supports that idea, but few clauses can also be read very widely, ref to clauses 6.5 and 8. 

Looking forward to your reflections on the above.

Cheers,

* they want all “reasonable data to determine and display estimated wait times and pricing” - basically they want to replace our dispatch. I’d suggest this is a hard NO

Hi Sten,

pleasure to e-meet you. I will try to tackle this one and offer you a framework for thinking about this 🙂 as I am afraid - I am not able to offer you a Yes/No answer. At least not such a Yes/No that would be still valid and relevant some time down the road.

From purely contractual approach and our promises made to drivers under T&Cs:

* indeed sec. 8.3 of the T&Cs as currently written obliges us a) constantly follow dynamics of driver - rating; → b) issue early-notice that rating falls below a certain minimum during certain window of time \[that driver needs to be aware of]

So drivers have a reasonable expectation that this is how blocking will happen and are able to raise issues (contractual challenges) if we fail to follow this logic.

Things get even more complicated if we check what the EU regulations require us to do in cases we block Driver’s access to platform/ability to do business and earn:

* if this is a full block → Bolt has to provide a statement of reason that is clear and specific 
* we have to give an early notice about full block → 30 days before blocking \[unless there is a reason to expect that not blocking immediately will cause more damage to passengers, us, etc.]
* we need to open-up a chance for Driver to rebuttal such block and file a complaint. We even have a complaint-handling-policy for that \[[https://bolt.eu/en/legal/complaint-handling-system-for-business/|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/complaint-handling-system-for-business/]]

So all in all both our current contract and EU legal protections give rise to drivers' expectations to both get a notice and a chance to have a say when it comes to him potentially being kicked-out the platform for reasons of poor ratings.

A bigger picture:

* I know that rules in Global T&Cs have not been fully mapped out against Product and Ops workings and policy → so this rule should not be given weight as setting a coherent thought-through course of action
* Global T&Cs (and thus local T&Cs that rely on Global → afaik all except UK + future DE) have been overdue for review and will be overhauled eventually. Legal team is setting up priorities to determine when the RH Global T&C overhaul can take place. This overhaul among other things will seek to put in place a defendable legal framework for taking actions against Drivers.

Let’s align your current investigations and efforts with T&C review plans and make sure Legal principles and Operational standard work well  together 🙂



Julius

          WHERE cp.payment_row_type = 'capture'

Hi Alex, Thanks for sending in the memos. 

I think in the future it would be most helpful to have a summary of your analysis upfront for each market 👍 This would help reduce the number or repeat questions/open ends in my review and would reduce unnecessary review for markets with clear red flags stopping consideration of them as LW. 

*For future: If in your review it is already clearly concluded that a market will not be eligible for a LWL, then there is no need for me to review further.* 🙂 

In those red light cases, I leave it for you to go back to the business and allow them to consider if this market will proceed with a standard launch given the red light items.  If that becomes the case, the business can initiate legals involvement as per a standard expansion once the market is approved to go.

*General Feedback to this Memo*:

I note that this information has all been obtained by a consultancy firm and not a law firm. In order to keep this process collaborative in the future it is crucial for legal that these memos are confirmed by a law firm qualified to provide legal advise on the local market. *Why?* If information provided through a consultancy is inaccurate, then we will only have our service agreement to rely on in follow up. Law firms, on the other-hand, carry liability for ensuring the legal advise they give to clients is accurate. From a cost and time side, it continues to make sense that this is a collaborative effort, however, we hope that you will understand and agree to utilise law firms for these reviews going forward. 👍 🙂 

Also, I find the feedback by this consultancy to be very general and in many cases avoiding giving directly the legal advise that we need to make our decisions. It is strongly preferred that these memos consider clearly only our LW approach and how it would be interpreted under local law/reg. From these, I am struggling to tell what they are concluding would apply to our services since everything seems to speak to ‘taxis’ in general, yet there is not really a clear conclusion that we would qualify as a taxi.

*Please find my comments below on each specific market:*

*Qatar:*  Overall, it is *not* my impression this is a LW eligible market.

This is because:

* they have expressed that we need to obtain a license to operate a RH platform through a local entity;
* Free zone entity options (_need more info on what this is_) still seems to require local representation and comes with a large annual fee not consistent with LW approach;
* Requirement for drivers to be employed by a licensed operator implies either we need to become an operator and employ them or that we need to contract with fleets. It was not clear to me what they were suggesting for us but note that working with fleets is generally a no-go from the LW approach. If otherwise the market would work for you (I think not) then we could consider this as a last resort through I strongly things with no local rep or payment processing this would not be feasible. 

This overview for me seems to leave a lot of questions unanswered and some of the input seems unclear and unsupported. For instance: How can there be no RH regulations but a legal obligation to obtain a RH license? 🤔 However, if you too conclude that this does not fit LW then probably there is not point further following up for clarity at this time.

My impression is that due to the operating legal requirements this market is instead open for consideration in the future with a local partner or a standard expansion approach which included Bolt local representation.

*Kuwait:* Overall, it is *not* my impression this is a LW eligible market (_though this memo particularly was very unclear and didn't seem to reflect on how the LW service is offered_).

This is because:

* Though they imply that obtaining a license to operate as a taxi operator may be an option, for Bolt this would go against all our standard operating practices (employing drivers, being liable for services etc). Therefore this option seems clearly off the table for us, LW or not.
* The memo seems to imply that we must have local entity regardless, though this is a bit unclear. If not, then this still may be an option on the table. Please confirm.
* Since being an operator ourself is fairly unreasonable, contracting local operators (presumably fleets) seems to be the only option to access supply. Working with fleets is generally a no-go from the LW approach. If otherwise the market would work for you (I think not) then we could consider this as a last resort through I strongly things with no local rep or payment processing this would not be feasible. 

*UAE:* Overall, it is *not* my impression this is a LW eligible market.

*Dubai*: This is because:

* License to operate required for RH platforms is required and means we need too register an onshore company licensed by the Dubai Department of Economic Development. It seems offshore option may be possible for 5-10k (not clear).;
* All discounts and promos must be approved by the regulator and on12% of rides may be discounted (not clear what the ‘starting point’ here is though)
* 90K euro bank guarantee required.

*Abu Dhabi*: This is because:

* License to operate required for RH platforms is required and means we need a local subsidiary;
* 90K euro bank guarantee makes this ineligible for a LW approach;
* Other requirements like the price limiting etc (seems same as Dubai since it is national regulation)

----

Since my strong impression is that all three of these markets are not LW eligible, I don’t believe further investigation or support is needed on my side at the moment. If you disagree with this conclusion at all, please let me know. 

_Note a number of my comments in the memos are rather framed for internal review. If you will go back to them with any further review then I advise you clear my comments and reword whats relevant._

A2.1) Yes, the optimal solution is to have 'user_id' in all tables that are sharded. This allows Vitess to efficiently find which shards to lookup (otherwise it will probably have to send the query to all shards - scatter query). Smaller cost due to Functional Unique Vindex:
https://vitess.io/docs/reference/features/vindexes/#cost


A2.2) Docs indicate we can use this:
====
Shared Vindexes #
Relational databases encourage normalization, which allows the splitting of data into different tables to avoid duplication in the case of one-to-many relationships. In such cases, a key is shared between the two tables to indicate that the rows are related, a.k.a. Foreign Key.

In a sharded environment, it is often beneficial to keep those rows in the same shard. If a Lookup Vindex was created on the foreign key column of each of those tables, the backing tables would actually be identical. In such cases, Vitess allows sharing a single Lookup Vindex for multiple tables. One of these tables is designated as the owner of the Lookup Vindex, and is responsible for creating and deleting these associations. The other tables just reuse these associations.

An existing lookup_unique vindex can be trivially switched to a consistent_lookup_unique by changing the vindex type in the VSchema. This is because the data is compatible. Caveat: If you delete a row from the owner table, Vitess will not perform cascading deletes. This is mainly for efficiency reasons; the application is likely capable of doing this more efficiently.

As for a lookup vindex, it can be changed it to a consistent_lookup only if the from columns can uniquely identify the owner row. Without this, many potentially valid inserts would fail.

Functional Vindexes can be also be shared. However, there is no concept of ownership because the column to keyspace ID mapping is pre-established.
====
https://vitess.io/docs/reference/features/vindexes/#shared-vindexes


A2.3) If the table that does not have user_id key is small, it can remain unshared and materialised into the sharded keyspaces for local joins:
====
Reference tables #
Vitess allows you to create an unsharded table and deploy it into all shards of a sharded keyspace. The data in such a table is assumed to be identical for all shards. In this case, you can specify that the table is of type reference, and should not specify any vindex for it. Any joins of this table with an unsharded table will be treated as a local join.

Typically, such a table has a canonical source in an unsharded keyspace, and the copies in the sharded keyspace are kept up-to-date through VReplication.
====
https://vitess.io/docs/reference/features/vschema/#reference-tables

netmonitor is SRE-s prometheus. It’s scraping two sources:

* netping - see EC2 instances netping-1a, 1b, 1c
* upstream-discovery - e.g. exporter from all LIVE node-servers, frontend and apache servers. see ec2 tag “exp_discovery”


The history why we have netmonitor separated from monitor.internal is following:

First we did had only one Prometheus instance which was monitor.internal. Because we where exited about Prometheus instead of old school metrics collecting like munin, we suggested to our CTO to implement prometheus exporter to our nodejs codebase so developers could have option to add any kind of business metrics they need to. So we created new Prometheus instance called nodemonitor.internal (node as nodejs). It took only one year and we ran nodemonitor on very large EC2 instances and started to look around for better solution. Then we assigned one new engineer to solve this issue and we end up with Thanos cluster. At about the same time we had trouble with AWS networking (it was time when 5 gen instances appeared; c5, m5). So we developed solution which did udp ping 2 times per second and exported the results to Prometheus. Because we did had need to have also 3 different source EC2 servers for netping we created netmonitor.internal to AZ 1c (other prometheus instances where on AZ 1a and 1b at the same time). So netping prometheus was collecting netping metrics and also was one of the source host of netping service. Later on I added also upstream discovery metrics there. At about the same time when nodemonitor was upgraded to Thanos I searched new hosts for netping and found out that we need to run them at least c5.large instances so the network jitter is minimal. So I created netping-1a,1b,1c for netping service. Corresponding service is netpong which is running on hosts where ec2 tag is “netmon: 1”

Re IP rights, our initial wording should remain. This is very standard clause for IP regulations. You mention that once Ignitis transfers all the rights to Bolt, it can not grant the licence on the top of that as the rights are already transferred. This is not the case: Ignitis is not granting a license on top of the transferred rights. How it works is that rights that can be transferred, such as economic rights, are transferred to Bolt, and rights that cannot be transferred, such as moral rights, are not transferred but the licence is granted to Bolt. Moral rights to which the license is granted should include the right of integrity and making a work available to public as well, which is currently striked through by Ignitis. 

Also, you do not need a separate transfer act for passing the IP rights. The rights are transferred with the agreement.

          ,target
          ,CASE

              WHEN ad_insights.campaign_name LIKE 'Riders, Scooters\%%'  THEN TRIM(' ' from split_part(split_part(ad_insights.adset_name, ',', 4), '(', 1))
              WHEN ad_insights.campaign_name LIKE 'Rider\%%' AND lower(ad_insights.campaign_name) LIKE '\%%installs\%%' THEN TRIM(' ' from split_part(split_part(ad_insights.adset_name, ',', 3), '(', 1))
              WHEN ad_insights.campaign_name LIKE 'Eater\%%' AND lower(ad_insights.campaign_name) LIKE '\%%installs\%%' THEN TRIM(' ' from split_part(split_part(ad_insights.adset_name, ',', 3), '(', 1))
              WHEN ad_insights.campaign_name LIKE 'Courier\%%' THEN TRIM(' ' from split_part(split_part(ad_insights.adset_name, ',', 3), '(', 1))
              WHEN ad_insights.campaign_name LIKE 'Driver\%%' AND lower(ad_insights.campaign_name) LIKE '\%%conversion\%%' THEN TRIM(' ' from split_part(split_part(ad_insights.adset_name, ',', 3), '(', 1))
              WHEN ad_insights.campaign_name LIKE 'Driver\%%' AND lower(ad_insights.campaign_name) LIKE '\%%remarketing\%%' THEN custom.main_city
              WHEN ad_insights.campaign_name ILIKE '\%%post eng\%%' THEN custom.main_city
              WHEN ad_insights.campaign_name ILIKE '\%%- post\%%' THEN custom.main_city
              WHEN ad_insights.campaign_name LIKE 'Rider\%%' AND lower(ad_insights.campaign_name) LIKE '\%%app engagement\%%' THEN custom.main_city
              WHEN ad_insights.campaign_name LIKE 'Driver\%%' AND lower(ad_insights.campaign_name) LIKE '\%%app engagement\%%' THEN custom.main_city
              WHEN ad_insights.campaign_name LIKE 'Business\%%' THEN trim(' ' FROM(SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(ad_insights.campaign_name,',',3),' - ',1)))
              WHEN ad_insights.campaign_name LIKE 'Branded\%%' THEN TRIM(' ' from split_part(split_part(ad_insights.campaign_name, ',', 4), ' - ', 1))
              ELSE TRIM(')' FROM TRIM('(' FROM TRIM(' ' from split_part(split_part(ad_insights.adset_name, ',', 3), '(', 1))))
              END AS city
        FROM (
              SELECT
                  adsets.name AS adset_name,
                  adsets.account_id,
                  adsets.id AS adset_id,
                  campaigns.id AS campaign_id,
                  campaigns.name AS campaign_name,
                  CASE WHEN campaigns.name LIKE 'Riders, Rental\%%' THEN TRIM(SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(campaigns.name ,',',3),'-',1))
                       WHEN campaigns.name LIKE 'Riders, Scooters\%%' THEN TRIM(SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(campaigns.name ,',',3),'-',1))
                       WHEN campaigns.name  LIKE  'Rider\%%' THEN TRIM(SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(campaigns.name ,',',2),'-',1))
                       WHEN campaigns.name  LIKE 'Driver\%%' THEN TRIM(SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(campaigns.name ,',',2),'-',1))
                       WHEN campaigns.name  LIKE 'Eater\%%' THEN TRIM(SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(campaigns.name ,',',2),'-',1))
                       WHEN campaigns.name  LIKE 'Courier\%%' THEN TRIM(SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(campaigns.name ,',',2),'-',1))
                       WHEN LOWER(campaigns.name ) LIKE '\%%post engagement\%%' THEN TRIM(SPLIT_PART(campaigns.name ,'-',1))
                       WHEN LOWER(campaigns.name ) LIKE '\%%- post\%%' THEN TRIM(SPLIT_PART(campaigns.name ,'-',1))
                       WHEN campaigns.name ILIKE 'Branded\%%' THEN TRIM(SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(campaigns.name ,',',3),'-',1))
                       ELSE TRIM(SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(campaigns.name ,',',2),'-',1))
                       END AS ads_country,
                  CASE WHEN campaigns.name LIKE 'Riders, Rental\%%' THEN 'Demand - Scooter'
                       WHEN campaigns.name LIKE 'Riders, Scooters\%%' THEN 'Demand - Scooter'
                       WHEN campaigns.name LIKE 'Rider\%%' THEN 'Demand'
                       WHEN campaigns.name LIKE 'Driver\%%' THEN 'Supply'
                       WHEN campaigns.name LIKE 'Eater\%%' THEN 'Eater'
                       WHEN campaigns.name LIKE 'Courier\%%' THEN 'Courier'
                       WHEN campaigns.name LIKE '\%%Business\%%' THEN 'Business'
                       WHEN campaigns.name ILIKE '\%%post engagement\%%' THEN 'Social Media'
                       WHEN campaigns.name ILIKE '\%%- post\%%' THEN 'Social Media'
                       WHEN campaigns.name ILIKE 'Branded\%%' THEN 'Branded Content'
                       ELSE 'Other'
                       END AS target
                  FROM adsets
                    INNER JOIN (
                      SELECT
                      adsets.id AS inner_adset_id,
                      adsets.account_id,
                      MAX(date_part(epoch, updated_time::timestamp) ) AS latest_date
                      FROM adsets AS adsets
                      GROUP BY 1,2
                    ) AS inner_adset on inner_adset.inner_adset_id = adsets.id
                      AND inner_adset.account_id = adsets.account_id
                      AND inner_adset.latest_date =date_part(epoch, updated_time::timestamp)


        LEFT JOIN
                  (
                    SELECT
                    campaigns.account_id,
                    campaigns.name,
                    campaigns.id
                    FROM campaigns
                    INNER JOIN (
                        SELECT
                        campaigns.id AS inner_adset_id,
                        campaigns.account_id,
                        MAX(date_part(epoch, updated_time::timestamp) ) AS latest_date
                        FROM campaigns AS campaigns
                        GROUP BY 1,2
                      ) AS inner_campaign on inner_campaign.inner_adset_id = campaigns.id AND
                        inner_campaign.latest_date =date_part(epoch, updated_time::timestamp)
                        AND inner_campaign.account_id = campaigns.account_id
                    ) AS campaigns ON adsets.account_id = campaigns.account_id
                      AND adsets.campaign_id = campaigns.id
        )
        AS ad_insights
       LEFT JOIN custom on custom.country = ad_insights.ads_country{code}

I’ve responded, in turn:

(1) There is no legal requirement to offer an opt-out. The legal basis for recording is “legitimate interest” - and we do not rely on consent. It follows, to be clear, that no consent is required to record inbound CS calls.

The caller does, however, have rights. They might object (or try to opt-out). Happy to deal with these instances case-by-case after the termination of the call.

Another right, mentioned above, is the right to be informed: you’ve said above that at the start of the call there is a message explaining the call is recorded (and that message should also say for what purpose the recording is for, and provide a steer to the Bolt website and the Privacy Policy “for more info”). 

(2) Both options work. 

The first option is preferential: again, we do not rely on consent but rely on legitimate interests to record and we inform callers of the recording.  and should they wish to object then, fine, they can.

I’d see the script like this:

Agent: “Before we go on, this call is recorded for the purpose of \[e.g. some legitimate interests like making sure we meet your needs]. The recording is in compliance with data protection rules. More information about how Bolt looks after customer data is available in the Privacy Policy available on our website. Are you happy to continue?”

In the event that the caller refuses to continue because of the recording, and the CS agent is comfortable not recording the call, then fine. The CS agent can instead provide a write-up or whatever of the call.

That’s the end of the responses to (1) and (2) above.

Let me know if you have further questions or any clarifications are required. Happy to jump on a call for this.

Please also be minded to consult with the local licensing terms with TfL which might contain specific telephony requirements unrelated to data protection rules.

_As advised, there are no specific RH laws and data protection laws in Pakistan are currently in draft form. However, if any personal identity information of users or drivers is retained by Bolt through the App, permission should be obtained from the users / drivers and measures should be taken that such information is not leaked out to the public._

_The relevant provisions that stipulate these requirement is in the Pakistan Electronic Crimes Act, 2016 (_*_PECA_*_). Under Section 16 of PECA it is an offense to “obtain, sell, possess, or transmit” identity information without authorization of the concerned individual. An offense under this section is punishable with imprisonment of up to three years, or a fine of up to Rs. 5 million, or both. Therefore, if Bolt makes such use of identity information of its drivers or users through the App, the concerned individuals should be informed and consent to such usage of their information._

# Payment Terminals are not exclusively offered by iZettle. Drivers can also use payment terminals from other parties in order to accept terminal payments in the Netherlands. Those drivers that we have encouraged to adopt this payment method, we have pointed towards iZettle. The drivers then independently signed up directly with iZettle, we are not involved in this process. These payment terminals enable drivers to accept Contactless Debit payments (as well as creditcard maestro), which is the main method of payment in the Netherlands. We have used the Cash Product infrastructure to enable terminal payments. Please read this [playbook|https://docs.google.com/document/d/17xAKfHgjN1Bv4JSRybrgM4ZFaaDh9ww-Mvqx5Aywz20/edit?usp=sharing] for further information on how this was implemented: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/17xAKfHgjN1Bv4JSRybrgM4ZFaaDh9ww-Mvqx5Aywz20/edit?usp=sharing|https://docs.google.com/document/d/17xAKfHgjN1Bv4JSRybrgM4ZFaaDh9ww-Mvqx5Aywz20/edit?usp=sharing|smart-link] 
# Terminal Payments indeed work exactly like cash as we have utilised the Cash infrastructure to set this up. This means that Drivers receive the payment from the rider on their payment terminal, which is then directly transferred to their bank account. Consequently, the drivers owe us the commission, which is compensated with in-app payments. There is an integration available with iZettle, but this will also be discussed in the negotiation as soon as the NDA is signed.
# The ~20% GMV I mentioned, which is now ~30% of total GMV is the percentage of GMV generated through this payment method: Terminal Payments. This is not exclusively iZettle. According to our tracking log, 67% of terminal payments are processed by iZettle and 33% by other providers. The negotiation for lower transaction costs would lead to lower cost for drivers. The revenue share model would lead to financial benefit to us (Bolt). They would be sharing revenue with us.
# Both iZettle and us, would be disclosing information to each other in order to negotiate a deal. However, having our NDA reviewed by Paypal, who is now restructuring its organisation as it acquired iZettle, would according to iZettle take many months. By that time, our chance for negotiation will be lost as the threshold to switch to another provider will be too high if the adoption rate of iZettle terminals continues at this pace. In the past 1 month, the GMV of this  payment method has increased from ~20% to ~30% of total GMV and the adoption of iZettle payment terminals is continuing. We are in a strong position for negotiation now, so it is essential for us to start the negotiation as soon as possible.

I hope this answers your questions in detail and I hope we can move forward with this NDA so we can negotiate a deal now we still have strong leverage. 

Please let me know if you have any concerns as to the content of the NDA so I can take this up with iZettle immediately.

Great Q and, yeah, let’s try and find a workaround\!

I think there is a really strong legitimate interest in sharing details with Fleet but, you’re both right, we can’t because there is likely not a reasonable expectation to share those details (so the LIA would fail).

I see two options:

# At the application stage, prior to submission, to state clearly something like, “After we’ve reviewed your application as a Driver, Bolt may share your personal data with a Fleet operator where doing so would be more appropriate to your circumstances. A Fleet operator may contact you to continue your application as a Driver where this is the case”.  If we’re sharing often then we’d quickly arrange for DPAs with the Fleet operators. The grounds for sharing are Legitimate Interests (we’d have established the applicant’s reasonable expectations for sharing with a Fleet operator for a well-grounded purpose”. Alternatively:
# When we reject an applicant for “no car”, we reach out with a template response. Something like, “A Fleet operator is a more appropriate application route for your circumstances because you do not own a vehicle.  We can share your details with a Fleet operator who will instead consider your application. The Fleet operator may contact you. If you are happy for us to share your details, please respond… \[etc etc]”

Both circumstances are based on legitimate interests with no consent management required (even though option 2 seeks an indication, it’s simply establishing an expectation). Both scenarios, I’m satisfied, fall outside the scope of Direct Marketing.

Hi Paul\! 

I have reviewed the NDA and will provide you my feedback below. However, I want to initially highlight to you that with the information you have provided this seems to be quite a *high risk* engagement. Discussing with CityBike potential financing, co-branding, and expansion runs the risk of a) carrying competition law risk as discussing sensitive operation plans or information with a competitor is generally prohibited and b) confidentiality risk for both parties (especially if partnership does not proceed) since the perception of either party could be that the information has been used to enable and grow the others business. 

I expect that this has already been considered in deciding to move forward with these discussions but incase not, please consider such risks in your decision.

*Purpose:* In these high risk cases, it needs to be clear what the purpose of the engagement is. This way, it does not leave open the chance for the counter-party to creatively misinterpret the permitted use of the information they receive or vice versa.

I would recommend the following:

_For the evaluation of a potential collaboration between the parties on vehicle financing, co-marketing services, and app-integration in \[VARIOUS EUROPEAN MARKETS? /GlOBAL MARKETS? /SPECIFIC MARKETS?]_

Paul, Please clarify the above scope and confirm this is accurate.

*Penalty*: It is worth considering if adding a penalty clause for disclosure is beneficial in such a high risk cases. Benefit to such a clause is increased deterrence from breach and a clear monetary claim value in the event of breach (helps in cases where damages from the breach can be hard to quantify). However, note the risk that as this is a mutual NDA where we are receiving information as well, this penalty would also be applicable to us if we misused the information they give us as well.  

Paul, please consider if we should include such a clause and if so, then if this information was to be misused how large the potential impact could on us could be? IE: In case of breach, what penalty would be reasonable in your view? EUR 5000 per breach? Greater or less?

*Regarding the general template changes you flagged:*

* *Term*: 5 years is not preferred, but is okay: Just note this is mutual so both parties will be limited accordingly. Risk is that this gives them longer to potentially claim our abuse of the information if the partnership does not proceed. 
* *Jurisdiction*: France jurisdiction as previously expressed is not our preference. In case of dispute it would be troublesome/more costly. We would far prefer the alternative to Estonia is UK. However, the alternative has already been rejected and this is the only option then just note that accepting it means accepting the risks/challenges above.

Hello Hannah,

Thanks for your response and good questions. I’ll try to answer them below to the best of my ability:

The registration / compensation structure should be really simple, but I guess we may have to split it into two agreements; one for financial support vs. one for admin/operational support. 
Financial will literally just be a donation to us at Bolt - which goes directly to the initiative. 
Adming / Ops agreement is more tricky, as I guess we need a contract for partners who’d be willing to share our codes via their services. This means we are basically giving codes to our partners, who in turn will share them with their users. For example, a digital med-tech company sending a code within its receipt for the patients vaccination booking confirmation. 

* Limitations: we’ll try to set geo-fencing on the codes to individual centers (so they can only be used for that particular destination). If that’s not possible, it’ll literally be a free ride for someone where we’re hoping there won’t be any fradulent behaviour. However, in any of the cases for this, there can never be any guarantees that fradulent usage of these codes won’t happen. I’ll explain more on this tomorrow if you want. 

* relationship to beneficiaries: not exactly determined, so happy to discuss this. From our perspective, we’d rather give a generic code to our partners, which we may update every other day or so to decrease risk of fraud, which they then can seed out through their channels. So technically it’s us handing codes to our partners. They then are responsible for the distribution to beneficiaries. But again - this is our desire. Let’s defo discuss this tomorrow. 

* It’s a one-time investment I reckon. If the same company wants to invest twice, I’d rather write double contracts given the high figure investmens we’re aiming for. 

* Both codes & credit - if possible. Reason being is that some of our partners represent the most senior in society. They may not want, nor be able to, install and use Bolt properly. However, our partner (a senior organisation), are willing to help them if we can support via Ride Booker (our B4B booking system). So that’ll probably require a credit solution. But the main idea for all other partners is to use codes. 



Hope this help answer some of your questions at least. I know many of above answers are a bit lofty. Simply because the project is still so fresh and not necessarily planned so we kind of need to invent this initiative as we’re launching it. I reckon it’ll be immensely helpful to get your thoughts on this tomorrow. Looking forward to our chat\!
