Let's take a step back and look at the bigger picture before deciding what to do with this Telia piece. 

*@nick*, [~accountid:5b18f5574bec0e53fdb555d5], and [~accountid:5c987f2c0cf73c3215ff6aa7] (for infosec) *- please guide on the way forward.* Also, do let me know if you'd like for me to schedule a quick call to discuss/ decide upon this.

Roughly *we repeatedly face four types of Customer documentation we're requested to sign*:

# *codes of conduct* applicable for suppliers, related to anti-bribery, environmental sustainability etc - often declarative and rather general. _Though in some cases the requirements can also be very detail, the Telia piece being a great example here starting with extensive anti-bribery obligations_ [_https://www.telia.ee/images/documents/juhendid/est/korruptsioon_valtimise_lepinguklausel.pdf_|https://www.telia.ee/images/documents/juhendid/est/korruptsioon_valtimise_lepinguklausel.pdf] 
# *NDA's*
# *infosec requirements* _The Telia piece at hand being an example of this._
# *standard documentation for purchasing (transportation) services* regulating issues up to fee for services, payment and termination terms etc. _Good example is the US Government's documentation for purchasing transportation services for their embassies. But again, also Telia provides a massive amount of documentation which should be reviewed by us in full:_ [_https://www.telia.ee/partnerile/tarnijale_|https://www.telia.ee/partnerile/tarnijale]



However, the first and second typically pose no major issue - we can comply - and those docs can mostly be signed after a quick sanity check only.

* Third group might set requirements we do not (or can not) comply with fully.
* Also the fourth one is often massive in size, provides conflicting rules to what is already included in our T&C, and typically treats Bolt as a classical transportation service provider.

*What shall we do about it?*

*(A)* As the single most practical risk is Customer terminating the B4B agreement with us then *the most bold route would be to just sign whatever is put forward by the customer as long as it's not fully off the point*. Theoretical risks (foremost claiming damages) would remain which are nearly impossible to map out comprehensively in advance, or

*(B) we decline signing Customer docs* as the service should be provided solely on providers docs, thereby risking losing business - is it really realistic at all? Or,

*(C)* we sign Customer docs, but only in parallel with an *addendum manifesting the key clauses where our docs take priority* over Customer's (should there be a conflict), e.g in terms of liability (incl monetary limits, excluding any liability for drivers omissions other than our obligation of taking reasonable steps to check the compliance of laws by the driver), scope of acceptable auditing, uptime SLA's, infosec etc (full list of the critical matters tbd). _We might be able to re-use some stuff from Bolt Food major partner engagements on this, or vice versa._



In order to get those Customer requests over the line quickly without exposing Bolt to major risk Legal would go with (C) in each case where there is a risk of non-compliance or conflict of clauses.

* _That would allow us to save resources without discussing each Customer requirement in depth, but would require some initial drafting from Legal and input from other badgers, incl from Tarmo for infosec etc._
* _In many cases that would likely be enough for Customers as often our contact points really just need to demonstrate for their internal records that their doc as such has been signed._



*Next steps?*

* would be great to have clarity from the stakeholders on the above
* reflect the decisions made in this [contracting playbook|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/2923561494/Contracting+playbook.+Major+Customers], incl definition to be provided for a "major customer" (if relevant) @nick
* apply it in practice starting with the Telia ticket.

*SUMMARY*

This still appears at the planning stages of a data sharing arrangement. I’m calling out now that no “promise” should have been afforded to officials prior to the purpose being better documented. There is no detailed proposal attached. I’m confused in terms of where all the work is on this project. I’m concerned the OC advice doesn’t detail the legality of any effects on drivers - perhaps there are none, but we have licenses in other markets which may be threatened by any breach of international norms or perceived mistreatment of drivers in Ukraine.

The proposal likely can be done - but it needs to be documented. The questions which follow should help establish the facts necessary to draft the necessary documentation: 

*QUESTIONS*

The following are Qs to help clarify some details. Crucially, we appear - *still(\!)* - to be stuck at what the purpose is, and how the purpose will be accomplished. Can you please attend to the following in order to remedy this? 


# Bolt will disclose to MIA (or a related party) the identity of all named drivers on the platform in Ukraine. Is this correct? Bolt will share: 

* Name
* Driver license number
* Car title
* Tax number

What is “car title”? What does this mean? And is the tax number really necessary for MIA to identify the individual? Do you have any written details of why these data points in particular were promised/why they are all required to identify the person on the MIA system?

2. MIA will match the disclosed driver details with its own dataset on violations of “speeding and other traffic rules”. MIA will return any associated data: identity + violations of speeding offences and other traffic rules”. Is this correct?


3. Is the return of the MIA data likely to be  accurate? Is the assumption that the registered Driver on the Bolt App is also the party who has committed the speeding violation from the MIA dataset reliable? Is there any possibility that this association may be incorrect?

4. Now in receipt of the MIA data, Bolt’s intention is to use the data to “reduce traffic offences in Ukraine and improve safety,” according to the current draft of the NDA. Your OC states that “This information \[from MIA] will be further used by Bolt on its own discretion”. Perhaps - but it needs to be documented. So let’s get this right: Where the MIA data identifies a Driver who has violated a speeding or other traffic rule, Bolt can fairly assume that the Driver poses a higher risk to the safety of passengers. Is this correct? As such, Bolt wishes to take corrective measures to help mitigate those higher risks associated with that named Driver. In doing so, this will help “reduce traffic offences in Ukraine and improve safety”. Is this correct? 

5. Now that Bolt recognises a risky Driver, it can be argued that there is a legitimate interest in taking corrective measures with a view to reducing offences and improving safety. What are those corrective measures? At this stage we need particulars. For example, will Bolt communicate to the Driver that it has been made aware of a speeding violation and remind the driver of safety standards and behavioral expectations? Will Bolt ask for the Driver to read in-app messaging concerning behavioural expectations and/or ask the Driver to review training material? Will the Driver be warned that Bolt is aware of a violation (bearing in mind your response at \[3] above)? Will there be punitive measures such as penalties from Bolt? Will the Driver be suspended or blocked from the App? What complaints or appeals mechanism, if any, do you intend to rely on fro any dispute with the Drivers? 

These proposals should be documented now for review now.

6. As Silja said, can you confirm whether the data from MIA constitutes criminal offence data in Ukraine? Bearing in mind that Ukraine is not party to the GDPR, I suggest a condition in the UK GDPR is identified as an international norm for justifying the intrusion into criminal offence data if required. I appreciate that this may not have been a concern for local OC, but there is a bigger picture, and wider risk to the business beyond the borders of Ukraine, with this sort of proposal. E.g. it could spark a formal enquiry in Tallinn.


*Other considerations:*

# The disclosure of all Bolt drivers and their details to MIA appears excessive on first consideration. That said, there are international norms in regulated markets for making similar disclosures and it may be argued that Bolt is simply replicating and providing a self-regulated model. If this remains the only means to match the data then I suggest a technical fix to psedonomise or hash the data is considered. Upon completing the draft sharing arrangement, please involve Tarmo in the discussions with the local team/MIA re: the transfer mechanism to be used.

# If it is the vehicle that has been subject to a speeding offence on the MIA dataset, and not a named Driver per se, then Bolt is likely to cause a data breach in making an unfair assumption. What’s more, complaints may arise where drivers dispute any assumption made by Bolt on violating speeding rules etc. Ensure that the matching is done so with confidence. And consider what the complaints procedure looks like. 

# You need to confirm with MIA the frequency of the data sharing to help prevent duplication of records. For example, if Bolt discloses driver details each month, then the returned data from MIA should only disclose violations of speeding and other traffic rules for that same month. Please also attend to retention rules.

*Next steps:*

Local team to answer Qs I’ve posted above; those answers should provide the information that needs to be documented. 

I’m handing this over to Silja as Counsel to ensure appropriate documentation is populated by local team. 

The documentation - forming a proposal - can then be taken to the MIA in order to discuss the transfer mechanism. Include Head of InfoSec, Tarmo, at this stage.

Hi. Had a chat with Murad yesterday - will outline a brief and action points below:

*Urgency*: no real urgency. More a nice-to-have to address some of complications Fleet-ops team is facing.

*Current Situation:* currently fleets are being signed-up without a real process or flow. Unlike PL Team AZ team is not using [Fleet Landing Page|https://fleets.bolt.eu/signup?utm_campaign=bolt-fleets&utm_medium=header&utm_source=website] to collect leads and start onboarding process. Instead the team is setting face-2-face meetings with fleet owners, getting info they need during these meetings or get docs paper-mailed to them. After collecting all info they need (mostly about number of cars fleet commits, ownership of cars) ops-team creates [Fleet Portal |https://fleets.bolt.eu/login]account for Fleet Owner. Fleet owners do not sign anything, do not accept any T&Cs (including standard Drivers’). A commission rate that is set it seems on a fleet-by-fleet basis is not written anywhere and is communicated verbally it seems. The only legal terms interaction that happens in case of Fleets is fleet drivers downloading Drivers' App and accepting Drivers T&Cs before starting to drive.

*Issues*: team faces few challenges with such flow

(1) *Tax Authority*: requires fleets to show commercial arrangement between Fleets and Bolt. Local Ops team always suggests sending out link to standard driver T&Cs where sec. 2.7 says that Fleet Owner who registers account for fleet-drivers takes responsibility for each driver and is jointly liable with them for due performance. However, Tax Authority (rightfully) does not accept this and requires Fleets to show a proper commercial agreement between Bolt and Fleet that also indicates commercial conditions (aka applicable commission) they need for tax-liability audit/calculations.

(2) *Bolt - Fleet relations on Commission:* it seems that local Ops is using a “dynamic” approach to Commission applicable to Bolt and change its level from time to time. They do communicate (potentially via phone-call) new commission and give 7-14 days “notice” before it comes into force. Some fleet owners (again rightfully) are not ok with that and challenge that there is no contract between Bolt and Fleet and thus such commission increase is not ok. Also local team wanting to take actions against fleets (for fraud/misbehaviour) and wanting to block them - face similar challenge of fleets pointing out that there is lack of contract and Bolt cannot take such action.

(3) *Legal gaps:* there is no point in the flow / engagement where Fleets explicitly agree to our T&Cs or any other conditions. The only source of “binding nature” of our T&Cs towards fleets seems to come from a fact that Fleets are adding drivers who accept our T&Cs (as employees/dependants of fleets) and which say that both Fleet and Driver are jointly liable for all that is in the T&Cs. But this is non-intuitive, stretched and causes problems.

*Plans:* local team does not plan to onboard new fleets and instead plans to focus on developing existing (and thus improving their relations). Currently there are 55 fleets. With average commission of 11,5%. 

*Solution:* 

+_Short term immediate solution:_+ for now add a step to the process where Bolt <> Fleet owners signs special T&Cs when agreement is reached and before Access to Fleet Portal is granted. These T&Cs should be in paper with wet-ink-signatures for Tax Authorities to let fleets off the hook. Due to small number of fleets and no immediate plans to grow it - seems acceptable from scalability perspective.

The fleet-agreement needs to contain the following:

* Indication that fleet owners accepts and is bound by Driver T&Cs and clearly accepts joint liability for all drivers it will add through the fleet portal
* Reps and Commitments to minimum standard (a) minimum 5 vehicles; (b) all Bolt branded <not clear who bears the cost>; (c) all vehicles added are owned by the Fleet Company
* Commission Fee (current) and procedure for changing it: 14 day notice - via e-mail? -  unilateral. If not accepted: termination notice from fleet <_Need to talk to JURIS here as he seems sceptical about spelling out commission fee and would like to have it vague “as notified by Bolt”_>

These Special T&Cs could be based on the approach in Bolt Food and the attached template (developed for launch in BY). But in short: short special T&C that point to general T&Cs and spell out essential commercial terms.

+_Long term solution_+_:_ once global Fleet terms are developed (mostly based on needs of markets like PL) they would be added to the Fleet Portal and fleet owners accessing the portal for the first time - would need to clearly consent to them. This would allow to get rid of written docs (at least for new fleets) provided that Tax Authority would be happy with viewing this as essential and sole commercial agreement between Fleet and Bolt.

To mitigate the issue to some extent we can:

# add finite number of automatic retries for config fetching after user logs in;

That data may be processed from OpenDataBot side in batches, so there’s will be no need to enrich absent data in our car base manually or 1-by-1, but will be possible to use better instruments (like, iMacros), so it can be processed afterwards semi-automatically. *A3*
_What missing data we want from OpanDataBot:_

* _real validity status of car insurance_

*A4*
_Unfortunately, as an OpenDataBot - Bolt API integration is not an option from our side, 2nd next most effective/fast method is: we download dataset needed in form of .csv or .xlsx or .xls file and sent it to OpenDataBot. *A5*
_In case if we want to do something with that info in our admin (for example, add missing colors to car profiles) – then we will use received file to run macros and add such data in admin. _Yes, the purpose is to have more data about the cars to enhance the accuracy of the records held by Bolt, to be able to close deficiencies or inconsistencies in our records. _In terms of cars:_

* _it can help us to reduce labour cost, because we can semi-automate such processes_

checked around how other RH platform handle the direct-messaging treatment and disclosure. 

It seems that even for the most challenging jurisdictions with strict Secrecy of Correspondence laws - no specific legal language is added to the T&Cs so set some sort of specific legal treatment. I am guessing that this is post-GDPR effect where privacy laws set a clear treatment of correspondence data and added transparency requirements, etc.

This is what Uber says about accessing content of messages:

* *_Communication Data:_* _We enable users to communicate with each other and with Uber through Uber's mobile apps and websites. For example, we enable partner drivers and passengers as well as restaurants or delivery partners and delivery recipients to call each other, write text messages or send other files (usually without mutual disclosure of telephone numbers). In order to be able to provide this service, Uber collects some data about the calls, messages or other communications, such as the date and time of the communication and its content. Uber may also use this data for customer support (including resolving disputes between users), for security purposes, to improve our products and services, and for analysis._

I thus think that at least for now - we should also treat it as a privacy issue and  conduct GDPR assessment of legal grounds/needs; add disclosures required under the GDPR (explain what data, for what purposes we will use, etc.). And not to add any specific legal treatment for direct-messaging into our contract with an exemption of tricky jurisdictions UK / FR / DE in the future - for which I will conduct separate investigations.

As regards the posters, I can provide the following comment (under 2 hours), but if a more detailed response would be needed, then we will probably need more specific information about the structures to be erected and municipalities in question.

As a general rule, any sign that is outdoors in a public area (a sign/banner on a building (private or public)), including painted pavement (i.e, direction signs) or any poster stand/sign has to be approved/coordinated with the local municipality construction board (būvvalde) pursuant to respective municipality regulations. There are certain exceptions, though, but if Bolt wishes that the sign is actually visible (as opposed to paper form A4 page attached to the building wall/window with transparent “scotch” tape) then most likely you would wish to make it in such dimensions and form which would require approval. But unfortunately  there is no uniform law governing all territory of Latvia in terms of how these advertising signs/boards are approved. Each municipality adopts its own rules. For example, the applicable rules for Riga are here (in Latvian) - [https://likumi.lv/ta/id/263561-par-reklamu-izkartnu-un-citu-informativo-materialu-izvietosanas-un-afisu-stabu-un-stendu-izmantosanas-kartibu-riga|https://likumi.lv/ta/id/263561-par-reklamu-izkartnu-un-citu-informativo-materialu-izvietosanas-un-afisu-stabu-un-stendu-izmantosanas-kartibu-riga]. At the same time you mention also Liepaja, Daugavpils, Jurmala, etc..  

Thus each municipality will have its own rules and there may be slight differences, but overall the processes will be quite similar. Namely, in all cases a design/project will be required, which would need to be approved with the owner of the land or the building (or both), certain description provided and then that submitted to the construction board for its approval. In some cases that can be done via e-mail, in other cases in person submissions are accepted only, in some municipalities review may take between few days and weeks, in some may be longer. At the end the applicant receives a so called “ad passport” – approval to erect/put up the relevant material. There may be different template forms to be completed, in some cases they would wish to see the design/project in one file format, in some cases in other. Thus, we would have to look up the rules of each respective municipality in question and then evaluate if coordination is necessary and what has to be submitted.

If a poster (as in pic 2) is erected, it may potentially need even further construction/design project from perspective of construction laws (i.e. not just for the visual content on the sign, but for the structure itself). It depends whether foundation is required for such poster and if so how deep. We see that in pic2 the poster stand is bolted to the ground, but most likely there is some form of foundation underneath, and not just the pavement bricks. Potentially the relevant shopping mall owner has already constructed/approved the relevant poster/stand under the same construction permit as the shopping mall itself. In that case you would be merely changing the content on such structure and would only need the “ad passport” approved for your relevant content.

The charging station/ rack itself could be argued not to constitute advertising, but merely a structure. But then again, as with the poster stand  structure,  depending how “permanent”/”fundamental” it is, a construction permit may be needed.

Please also there are certain rules for charging stations –[https://likumi.lv/ta/id/297090-prasibas-elektrotransportlidzeklu-uzlades-dabasgazes-uzpildes-udenraza-uzpildes-un-krasta-elektropadeves-iekartam|https://likumi.lv/ta/id/297090-prasibas-elektrotransportlidzeklu-uzlades-dabasgazes-uzpildes-udenraza-uzpildes-un-krasta-elektropadeves-iekartam] (again, only Latvian version available currently).  They foresee the technical requirements for such stations insofar as the charging station is publicly available and provides a charging service. In either case, irrespective if there is actually a charging service provided (i.e. that I can pay a fee and charge my own non-Bolt scooter, vs I am merely asked to park a Bolt scooter at the station and potentially get a discount for such good behaviour for next rides) the station should be “safe” – i.e. there should not be risks of getting electrical trauma due to such object being out in the public.

Hopefully this is sufficient at this stage. If you need our help in exploring further the applicable rules across particular municipalities, then please let us know and we can then provide a further quote of fees based on the requested scope.

Have a good weekend\!

Kind regards,

{quote}The status of this denotes that this is a known vulnerability where risk might have been accepted. Could you provide more information and an assessment concerning this?{quote}

Delivery fee is calculated in our backend systems when the user searches for Restaurants in the Bolt Food app. Calculation of delivery fee depends on multiple dynamic variables e.g. distance from restaurants, courier availability, eligible campaigns or custom restaurant specific variables. That means consecutive calculations of a delivery fee for a particular user that wants to order from a specific restaurant *can not be guaranteed to be the same relative to time.*Therefore when Bolt Food was built & launched initially, it was agreed with Product & Engineering that when it comes to delivery fee, the process would be the following:
-> Backend system computes the delivery-fee once for each restaurant when user searches for restaurants
-> The delivery fee is sent to the Mobile app & stored there
-> When the user makes an order, the delivery fee that was initially received at search time is sent back to the backend system on checkout phase.
-> Backend system accepts the delivery fee as it is without any validation because it is not possible due to the way it is calculated.Adding validation on checkout phase would result in a high amount of mismatches between calculation of delivery-fee and our users would be notified frequently that our delivery price changes. It was also important for Product that our application would follow the pattern “User pays what he/she sees on the application & the price does not change along the way”

{quote}Is the vulnerability and risks as a result of it accepted? what was considered in acceptance?{quote}

The above approach presents the following risks:


* An attacker can use the checkout endpoint & modify the delivery fee however it wants and the system would accept it as it is as long as it’s a number.
* Accessing the checkout endpoint requires being authenticated on Bolt Food platform so an attacker can only use it if it has logged in with some credentials.
* The attacker can set the delivery-fee to 0 and receive his food orders without paying for delivery.
* The attacker can set the delivery-fee to a really high amount and this will result in charging the Eater (attacker in this case) the sum and Bolt receiving the money. The courier earning calculation is not dependant on the value of the delivery-fee that we receive from the attacker. So in this case, the courier will receive the amount he/she is entitled to and the excess money will come to Bolt.

Product Manager has been informed of the risks and has expressed multiple times that these are acceptable. Delivery fee amounts are relatively low so the impact of an attacker getting free delivery would be low. Repeating this pattern over-over would result in a higher impact but also the visibility for it would increase as we would see in our system that we have a high number of orders with 0 delivery fee that don’t have campaigns attached to it. The majority of 0 delivery fee in our systems are a result of campaigns.The best solution to this risk is adding a price locking mechanism which we have built on the Backend Side and it is ready for use. It requires integration with Mobile side which is under the responsibility of our Product Manager to plan it for development.

*_CGS is not processing the data (do not interpret/analyze), is not storing the data._*

*_\[Cornelia.Zorila] CGS is using dynamic IP allocation using ExpressVPN to protect the privacy and increase security. #!/bin/bash
# NRPE exit codes
# 0 - OK
# 1 - WARNING
# 2 - CRITICAL
# 3 - UNKNOWN

# number of hours since last update to alert on, defaults to 24
CRIT=${1:-24}

### CHECK VITESS LOG FILE
# check vitess log files for last restore date; logfile timestamp format does not have year, must inject it eg: I0416 01:11:12.55708
THISYEAR=$(/bin/date +'%Y')
LOGFILE_DATETIME=$(grep -i 'Restore: restarting mysqld after mysql_upgrade' /vt/log/vttablet.INFO | tail -n1 | cut -f1,2 -d' ' | sed "s/^I/$THISYEAR/")
SECS_SINCE_RESTORE=$(expr $(date +'%s') - $(date -d"$LOGFILE_DATETIME" +'%s'))

# exit with CRITICAL if restore age > CRIT threshold
# negative restore age means restore was last year, should self correct on Jan 2nd
MAX_SECS=$(expr $CRIT \* 60 \* 60)
if [ $SECS_SINCE_RESTORE -gt $MAX_SECS ]
then
    echo "CRITICAL - RESTORE TEST - restore older then $CRIT hours "
    exit 2
elif [ $SECS_SINCE_RESTORE -lt 0 ]
then
    echo "WARNING - RESTORE TEST - negative date, perhaps last restore was last year?"
    exit 1
fi

### CHECK LAST UPDATE IN MYSQL
# calculate how many hours since last update on a user owned table - under the vt_% schema
# information_schema_stats_expiry => https://bugs.mysql.com/bug.php?id=95407
SQL="SET SESSION information_schema_stats_expiry=0; SELECT MAX(UPDATE_TIME) from information_schema.TABLES WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA LIKE 'vt%' into @last_update; select HOUR(TIMEDIFF(NOW(), @last_update)) ;"

HOURDIFF=$(/usr/bin/mysql --socket=/vt/mysql.sock -BNe "$SQL" 2>/dev/null)
EXITCODE=$?

# mysql needs to return valid results otherwise alert
if [ $EXITCODE -ne 0 ]
then
    echo "CRITICAL - RESTORE TEST Can't connect to mysql"
    exit 2
fi

# check last update
if [ $HOURDIFF -gt $CRIT ]
then
    echo "CRITICAL - RESTORE TEST - restore older then $CRIT hours "
    exit 2
elif [ $HOURDIFF -lt $CRIT ]
then
    echo "OK - RESTORE TEST - restore less than $CRIT hours "
    exit 0
else
    echo "UNKNOWN- "
    exit 3
fi
